reason: B is the stronger proposal because it extends prior glass-to-glass-transition results to phosphorus-containing alloys with a controlled, falsifiable intervention, whereas A largely repeats the cited melt-spinning experiment and makes an inadequately supported claim that faster quenching increases thermal stability. B’s main weakness is that post-quench annealing can improve resistance to crystallization but not glass-forming ability in the strict sense of forming glass from the liquid.
